title: image-blaster: one image to an explorable 3D world, as a Claude Code skillset
author: Neilson K-S (@neilsonks)
desc: The author writes "open-sourcing a 3D gen toolkit for Claude Code" that turns an "input image → environment, meshes, physics, lighting, & audio". The repository describes "An image-to-world skillset for Claude": Claude Code runs skills and subagents that call World Labs' Marble for a Gaussian-splat environment, Hunyuan 3D through FAL for meshes of the dynamic objects, image-edit models for clean plates and ElevenLabs for ambient and object sounds, in "< 5 minutes" per its README. The thread [shows the skills harness](https://x.com/neilsonks/status/2055013784260059471), [explains that meshed objects are removed from the input image to build the static world](https://x.com/neilsonks/status/2055013786063691872), [adds a companion app to view and pose the objects](https://x.com/neilsonks/status/2055013788034945535) and [links the code](https://x.com/neilsonks/status/2055013789607879096); [a post the next day](https://x.com/neilsonks/status/2055384282148082087) invites people to share what they make. The clip pairs input images with the worlds made from them, such as an attic, a cellar with clay pots and a library, and shows the Claude Code session. The author's X profile lists product work at World Labs, whose Marble model the skillset calls. The repository dates from April and May 2026, earlier than most cases in this archive.
model: Claude (through Claude Code; the repository names no model version, and its subagents inherit the session's model)
tools: Claude Code; World Labs Marble; Hunyuan 3D through FAL; nano-banana and gpt-image-2 for image edits; ElevenLabs sound effects

title: AWSM: geometry-grounded agentic reconstruction, mapping and simulation
author: Yaofang Liu (@stephenajason)
desc: The authors introduce AWSM (Agentic World Simulation and Mapping). W. Wang's thread notes that agents "like #GPT6 #Astra can now build editable 3D scenes straight from visual observations" and that AWSM "grounds this agentic reconstruction in geometric evidence (IMU, metric depth and camera poses), so the resulting scenes can serve as maps and simulation assets for robots"; Yaofang Liu's post describes the multi-robot demo, in which "four robots follow predefined routes to reception and line up." The project page compares four routes, from RGB only to ground-truth camera poses, in one synthetic NVIDIA Isaac Sim lobby, and reports that bidirectional surface error falls from 0.376 m to 0.072 m; it adds that "One synthetic scene and one engineering run per route do not establish general superiority or statistical significance." The rest of the thread covers [the study and the robots](https://x.com/wenting_is_here/status/2105675341880779183), [real-to-sim-to-real](https://x.com/wenting_is_here/status/2105675387003183115), [a phone video of the team's café turned into an interactive Blender scene](https://x.com/wenting_is_here/status/2105686613695324221) and [the code](https://x.com/wenting_is_here/status/2105675551612821646), crediting "@stephenajason and Phygital AI Team"; [a quote post](https://x.com/stephenajason/status/2105680951489753109) by Yaofang Liu reads "GPT-6 Astra building 3D scenes is exciting." The clip moves from the lobby to a route map ("One map. One destination. Four robots."), the four robots at the reception desk and the café video beside its editable Blender scene.

title: Lab kitchen walkthrough video to 3D assets with joints (kitchen-twin)
author: Zhiyang (Frank) Dou (@frankzydou)
desc: An agentic workflow that turns one handheld phone walkthrough of a lab kitchen (~20 s) into 3D assets, with no depth sensor, CAD or asset library, in about a day including human-in-the-loop. The author's description of the loop: ViPE gives camera poses and metric depth; GPT-6 lists the objects, and open-vocabulary detection and tracking gives per-object masks; for every asset GPT-6 writes the object as a program in a small Blender DSL, renders it over the original frames, compares it with the scan points in 3D and iterates; a separate GPT-6 session is the verifier and "must justify every complaint with a frame"; the output is MJCF/URDF with joints. Author's caveats: "thin and shiny things are still weak, a few objects are drafts, the room shell needs another pass."

desc: The author writes "GPT6 Astraで動画を元に3Dを作成！！" (made 3D from a video with GPT-6 Astra): the top of the clip is a source video made with Midjourney and Kling, the bottom the 3D space built with it as reference, labelled "GPT-6 + Blender + Rodin". The author calls it "一回目の成果物" (a first result) with finer textures still to come.
tools: Blender; Hyper3D Rodin (per the clip's label); Midjourney and Kling for the source video

title: A kinetic pavilion based on Buckminster Fuller's jitterbug transformation
author: KOBATAKA｜Vibe Modeling (@shion_takk)
desc: The author starts on moving pavilions: "動くパビリオンを考えだす" (starting to think about a moving pavilion), based on Buckminster Fuller's "ジッターバグ変換" (jitterbug transformation). [The next post](https://x.com/shion_takk/status/2103655489989140934), captioned "Claude Opus 5.5｜Vibe Modeling（Blender）", presents a "ジッターバグ灯籠パビリオン" (jitterbug lantern pavilion) that opens and closes in response to the time of day, and notes that the model "自力で中心に球型ジョイントを入れる機構を発想して採用してくれた" (came up with, and adopted, a mechanism with a spherical joint at the centre by itself). The clips show the frame folding and the lit pavilion at night.

title: A kinetic pavilion folded on the Kresling origami pattern
author: KOBATAKA｜Vibe Modeling (@shion_takk)
desc: Captioned "Opus 5.5｜Vibe Modeling", the post presents a "Kresling折紙" (Kresling origami) pavilion that extends and contracts vertically. The author writes that several options were considered before a direction was chosen and refined, and that "図面表現は全然ダメなので改善が必要" (the drawings are no good at all and need improving). The clip and images show the twisting frame, its membrane roof and the pavilion in a park.

title: Monica's apartment from Friends as a recurring test: Opus 5 in Blender, then Astra, Grok 4.7, MiMo and Sol 6.1
author: Scott (@scottstts)
desc: The author first wrote "I asked opus 5 to make Monica's apt from Friends in Blender, it made this. I also rendered out a few images using cycles", with [Cycles renders](https://x.com/scottstts/status/2081031019302449173) in a reply. He then reran the subject as a Three.js test: GPT-6 Astra on 2026-09-04 ("[same monica's apt in @threejs test, this is by far THE BEST result i have seen](https://x.com/scottstts/status/2095979106156384438)", measured against his own reference build), [Grok 4.7](https://x.com/scottstts/status/2102101560645800222) ("the details are still lacking compared to astra/fable/opus"), [MiMo-V2.6-Pro](https://x.com/scottstts/status/2102325403881000962) ("Still not astra/fable level") and [GPT-6.1 Sol](https://x.com/scottstts/status/2105022854941052982), which he judges "roughly the same or even better" than Astra. Each clip walks through the purple living room, kitchen and furniture. The judgements are the author's; the posts publish no shared prompt.
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.7, MiMo-V2.6-Pro and GPT-6.1 Sol, same subject from the same author)

title: Conceptual X-16 engine in Three.js, with its source
author: Techartist (@techartist_)
desc: Techartist writes "Built a conceptual X-16 engine in 3D with GPT-6 Astra using Threejs. Four cylinder banks, one crankshaft and exposed mechanics inspired by experimental multi-bank engine architectures." The clip moves through an interactive page with hero, crankshaft, bank, cutaway and exploded views, piston details and a running crank. It is a conceptual mechanism visualization, not a validated engine design.

title: Particle-collider exhibit with a detector that comes apart
author: BuBBliK (@k1rallik)
desc: BuBBliK writes that "One prompt to Astra started a 3D particle collider. A few refinements turned it into 5,212 animated components you can take apart." The clip shows a detector opening layer by layer, a 27 km accelerator ring and a synthetic collision display. The repository calls it a conceptual visualization, not a physics simulation or official CERN software.
model: GPT-6 Astra (named Astra by the author)

title: An explorable male-anatomy model with separated parts
author: ashe (@ashebytes)
desc: ashe presents a GPT-6 Astra anatomy website. The author says it "pulls apart the male anatomy into 2,234 modeled pieces"; the post does not provide an independent part-count or anatomical-accuracy check. An author reply links the demo and the code. The repository README says the viewer uses "BodyParts3D 4.0, an adult male reference anatomy", with geometry simplified "while retaining every source mesh". The demo returned HTTP 503 "DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED" on 2026-09-28.

title: Cozy wetland lake: Blender assets to a Three.js world
author: Givros (@givros)
desc: Cozy wetland lake: Blender assets to a Three.js world
tools: Blender; GLB; Three.js; custom prompting workflow

title: Interactive lens lab: the plane of focus in 3D
author: Ryan Sael (@RyanSael)
desc: Ryan Sael writes "I asked Opus 5.5 to explain camera focus by building an interactive lens lab" and reports "1 hour 26 minutes in one shot, $25.66 API cost". The clip moves around a cutaway lens on a bench whose glass elements shift as the focus ring turns, while a plane of focus sweeps through a small landscape diorama, and then shows the image plane. The live page has focus, aperture and assembled or exploded lens controls. Time and cost are the author's figures.
demo_label: The Plane of Focus lens lab

title: Steam-locomotive drawing to an editable Blender model
author: Tom Krcha (@tomkrcha)
desc: An old drawing of a steam train, given to Astra to reconstruct in Blender. Author: "After few minutes it crafted 3,295 fully editable detailed objects with beautiful geometry." Level of detail can be requested.

title: Tugboat concept art to a Blender model in about 10 minutes
author: Emmanuel de Maistre
desc: Author: "GPT 6 built this studio-quality tugboat in @Blender from one Scenario image and one prompt, in about 10 min. Fully autonomous." A low-poly version "under 10k faces" followed "in 10 more minutes". Shawn Woods, sharing it: "There's a ways to go before they hit the quality of an artist, this is where human interaction comes in."

title: Ship modeled from scratch in Blender and rendered in 4K
author: Ben Davis (@davis7)
desc: The attached clip is "a full 4k render of a ship that it made from scratch in blender". The same post reports Astra doing project setup and color grades in Final Cut Pro and selections in Affinity Photo through computer use.
tools: Blender, Final Cut Pro, Affinity Photo

title: Server rack and data center: Blender to Unity to SynergyXR
author: Sune Wolff
desc: Workflow as described by the author: a server rack modeled in Blender from four reference photos; a data center from a single photo; 180 racks placed automatically in Blender; the FBX imported into Unity and built into a SynergyXR environment. "... no MCP servers, no plugins, no connections, and Astra never touched our computer directly." Weak spot noted: reference adherence on the first blockout.

title: Lakeside French village with a circular central square
author: Givros (@givros)
desc: Givros asks GPT-6 Astra Ultra for "a circular central square inside a roughly square village". The post describes a Codex-and-Blender workflow spanning layout, assets, rendering and visual inspection, with a video of the scene. Its requested checks are part of the brief, not independent proof that every geometric constraint was met.

title: Reference-guided Blender environment and cinematic
author: Gokula Krishnan P
desc: Gokula Krishnan P describes recreating an environment in Blender with ChatGPT Astra, including reference, composition, materials and details. The author calls the result "a complete 3D environment + cinematic video", and attaches the clip.

title: OP-1 Field modeled and rendered in Houdini through MCP
author: Nick Scarcella (@_nscr)
desc: Nick Scarcella says he "Had GPT-6 Astra model and render an OP-1 Field in Houdini via MCP." The post includes the product render and explicitly cautions "There's issues".

title: Porsche body: expert-guided subdivision topology
author: Tom Krcha
desc: Tom Krcha tests GPT-6 Astra on a Porsche body and asks whether it can model clean subdivision topology and soft shapes. His conclusion is "Naive prompts will fail, refined systematic prompts written by an expert succeed."
tools: Subdivision-surface modeling; Rhino visible in media (porschehull.3dm)

title: Kitchen assets, materials and lighting in Blender
author: AKANSHA DEVLI
desc: AKANSHA DEVLI presents an ASTRA-and-Blender kitchen-scene experiment. The author describes "3D asset generation from a simple prompt" and "Scene integration into a complete kitchen environment", with an attached process image.

title: Forest path in Blender: Astra and Fable compared
author: Satyam Kumar (@_satyam_ai)
desc: Satyam Kumar compares the two models on "Same brief: a forest path in Blender, 12 seconds each." The attached side-by-side clip is the task evidence; the author's proposed explanation about training data is speculation rather than a measured finding.

title: A personal bottle recreated as a 3D model
author: Dara A. (@daradoescode)
desc: Dara A. describes Astra making personal objects into "3d models". This post's object is "my LIMITED edition goblin bottle", shown in the attached model video.

title: GPU workstation photographs to Blender models and animated websites
author: Alexey Fateev (@superalesha)
desc: Alexey Fateev gives both models "four photos of my 4x3090 rig from different angles and access to Blender MCP." After reconstruction, he asks each for an animated website and attaches the comparison.

author: Techartist (@techartist_)
desc: Techartist presents an interactive engine model and explicitly credits "Code -> GPT-6 Astra". The author describes the subject as "The 9-cylinder radial engine"; the attached clip shows the browser visualization.

author: モジョン (@mojon1)

title: Interactive V8-engine visualization
author: Dilum Sanjaya (@DilumSanjaya)
desc: Dilum Sanjaya writes "Asked GPT-6 Astra to create a highly detailed, interactive visualization of a V8 engine". The attached video is the visualization evidence; no physical-engine or accuracy test is reported.
tools: No modeling tool or library named

title: Titan visualization with Astra Medium in Codex
author: Arda Tuğsat (@ArdaTugsat)
desc: Arda Tuğsat presents "Scientific 3D simulation of the Saturn's largest moon Titan". The caption credits "GPT-6 Astra Medium Reasoning in Codex"; scientific accuracy is not independently evaluated.

desc: Author: "Anthropic cooked with Opus 5.5" and that "its better than Fable 5.1 and Astra its little close to real one those tiny details: jaguar logo, sensors". The prompt was "3d model of Waymo autonomous vehicle (Jaguar I-PACE crossover SUV)", run with "Opus 5.5 max in Claude code". One author's side-by-side judgement, without a shared protocol or repeated attempts. The same author's [later post](https://x.com/HarshithLucky3/status/2101748269248614599) calling a video "Fake Opus 5.5 output" links a [YouTube video](https://youtu.be/AlMLFkN79dA) of a different project, a forest survival game, not this render.

desc: Author: "The prompt was to it to create a beautiful mechanical butterfly in three.js and needless to say the output is indeed beautiful! Earlier it was being tested under the placeholder "gemini-3.7-flash" but it seems to be have been removed from arena since." The model behind the output is not identified by its vendor.

Codename, settings and identity are all author-reported.
model: Unreleased checkpoint attributed to Gemini 4 Pro by the authors

author: Lumina (@LuminaBench)

Lumina's "PS5 SVG example" is a DualSense controller drawn as SVG that took "around 10 minutes to complete"; it is a two-dimensional illustration, not a 3D model or CAD geometry. Qwinah's clip shows an Arena battle-mode run in which the "gemini-3.8-flash" pane renders a 3D Formula 1 car written in Three.js; the author writes "this car prompt took roughly 2-3 mins, and is being ghost tested under 3.8 flash".

author: Techikansh (@techikansh)

The post quotes the same author's [model-attribution post](https://x.com/techikansh/status/2102483794032792062), which says "Opus 5.5 just killed one of my tests." The visualization's scientific accuracy is not established.

desc: The stacked clip shows balloon-lifted house models from changing viewpoints, labeled Opus 5.5, Opus 5 and GPT-6 Astra. The author states "Same prompt. Same reference. XHigh. One shot via @aimlapi." and reports "Opus 5.5: 36:46", "GPT-6 Astra: 32:12" and "Opus 5: 14:56". These are the author's run times and settings, not a matched independent evaluation.

desc: The video compares Formula-style cars on turntables, with Opus 5.5 labeled above and GPT-6 Sol below. The post also mentions Astra, but the video does not show a third Astra panel. The author's verdict is "Opus 5.5 delivered the best." The post does not publish the shared prompt or matching run settings.

title: Pink convertible models with on-screen model labels
author: Stefan 3D AI (@Stefan_3D_AI)
desc: The caption asks "Who has best ride lol..." without naming a model. The video labels the upper panel "Opus 5.5" and the lower panel "GPT-6 Astra", showing model construction followed by turntable views of two pink convertibles. The post supplies no shared prompt or matched run settings.
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra; attribution comes from the author's on-screen video labels)

title: Underwater submarine models: Astra and Opus
author: Dominik Scholz (@dom_scholz)
desc: Dominik Scholz compares "GPT-6 Astra vs. Opus 5.5", saying "the latter definitely needed way less handholding". The two labeled panels show illuminated submarine models underwater, with camera passes over their hulls, windows and lights. The amount of assistance is the author's qualitative assessment.

title: VANTA / 07: an original helmet built as an editable Blender object under art direction
author: Spenser Dickerson (@SpenserFX)
desc: The author frames an eight-part thread as "a study: can Blender MCP + Astra actually build some cool stuff?", starting from a generated image of an original helmet. He writes that "I had to firmly interject several times to have Astra practically start from scratch after the first 2 attempts", that random primitives, floating pieces and poor connections "wan't fully resolved in the end", and that Astra generated tileable textures on demand. [The last part](https://x.com/SpenserFX/status/2096382448988758379) concludes that the work ran "passively over the span of 3 hours and the results are fairly useable to an extent." The clip shows the helmet in Blender, its wireframe and a full-colour turntable beside an editable cage.

title: BRUTE: a gas mask in two colourways, from Blender build to Gaussian splats
author: Spenser Dickerson (@SpenserFX)
desc: The author calls it "my second human-directed, Blender study with GPT-6 Astra + Blender MCP": "Two colorways. UVs. Worn materials.", with Gaussian splats trained in LichtFeld Studio and real-time effects in SplatPaint. [One part of the thread](https://x.com/SpenserFX/status/2097014127965487151) says "The first pass rushed into a full build before the proportions worked" and that lessons from the first study "became a reusable skill: compare orthographic views, fix the weak part, preserve what works", although "a lot of coaching was still required"; [the last part](https://x.com/SpenserFX/status/2097015673280926083) describes 200 Cycles views per colourway exported through COLMAP into trained splats and links a case-study repository. The clip shows the mask in both colourways.
tools: Blender MCP; Blender; Cycles; COLMAP; LichtFeld Studio; SplatPaint

title: A vintage gym built to manufacturer specs over ten hours and 21 rounds of revisions
author: Spenser Dickerson (@SpenserFX)
desc: The author reports "About 10 hours, 21 rounds of revisions and 1.3M polygons. Vintage gym built with GPT-6 Astra driving Blender on a MacBook Pro." He singles out watching Astra "source manufacturer specs and technical drawings" for the hoop and flooring, and adds "Definitely not one prompt. Lots of art direction, refs and corrections." [A reply](https://x.com/SpenserFX/status/2097500694253105363) says Astra then used his Cinema 4D MCP to migrate the Cycles build and rebuild the shaders in Octane. The clip moves through the gym from the viewport to finished renders.

title: Teenage Engineering OP-1 field modelled in Blender from two prompts
author: Keisuke Oyama (@keisuke_oyama)
desc: The author tried Blender MCP as soon as Astra arrived and writes that it reached a moving level, from "Astra highの添付の2回の指示のみ" (only the two attached instructions, on Astra high). The screenshots show the chat, the synthesizer in the Blender viewport and the render; [a reply](https://x.com/keisuke_oyama/status/2096061304780079213) adds another rendered angle, notes that even the knob texture was reproduced, and says it is "完璧ではない" (not perfect) on close inspection.

title: OP-XY synthesizer rebuilt from six photos and one video, with animated scenes
author: Lee Black (@mrblackstudio)
desc: The author posts four renders captioned "GPT-6 Astra to Blender MCP test" and, in [a reply](https://x.com/mrblackstudio/status/2097087355739881788), "It also moves". [A later post](https://x.com/mrblackstudio/status/2097082023990960277) explains "6 photos. 1 video. That's all I gave ChatGPT 6 Astra as reference to rebuild my OP-XY in Blender via MCP and set animated scenes." The images and clips show close-ups of the keys, knobs, ports and screen.

title: A three-screen MacBook Pro Duo concept modelled in Blender
author: Lee Black (@mrblackstudio)
desc: The author first posts renders captioned "A new kind of Duo made in @Blender", then [explains](https://x.com/mrblackstudio/status/2100221665556734002): "Had the idea. Opened GPT-6 Astra. Connected it straight into Blender via MCP. Built it. No modelling skills. Just art direction → Blender = a MacBook Pro with 3 screens, a mag stand + doubles up as an extended display in any direction." The images show the folded device, its screens and the stand.

title: A cozy sushi shop diorama from a one-line prompt
author: bluedev (@blueemi99)
desc: The author writes "GPT-6 Astra is CRAZY in blender" and quotes the prompt: "make me a cozy sushi japanese shop in blender using its mcp, please make sure its as nicely as you can, with details and extreme quality". The render shows a lit shop with a tiled roof, noren curtains, a counter with stools and a menu board on a stone base. The post gives no time or iteration count.

title: A Slash metal card designed and animated in Blender for about $130 of API credits
author: Mason Warner (@masonwarner)
desc: The author writes that Astra "One shotted a near perfect Slash card off of a few images I uploaded" and [shows it](https://x.com/masonwarner/status/2096386632731791586) in Blender. [Two days later](https://x.com/masonwarner/status/2096776337965171060) he reports "Made this entirely with Astra + Blender MCP" and "Cost roughly $130 in API credits to design the card from scratch and then animate this video", adding "It's not perfect photorealism, but I only prompted a few times". [A later render](https://x.com/masonwarner/status/2098974355569177032) places the card on a rock for an updated Slash website hero, "Made entirely via the Blender MCP with Astra".

title: TIDELINE: a walkable room whose furniture can be picked up and turned
author: おのふみ| 3D×動画生成×個人開発 (@onofumi_AI)
desc: The author tests "GPT-6 Astra × Blender MCPで「歩ける3D空間」" (a walkable 3D space with GPT-6 Astra and Blender MCP): furniture can be taken out one piece at a time and rotated, the room can be walked through, and editable Blender data remains. The author notes that graphics were not the focus of this first test. The clip shows a page titled TIDELINE with the room, a sofa picked out of it and the interior view.

title: A desert canyon cinematic made by Claude with access to every MCP tool
author: Dhruval (@dhruvalgolakiya)
desc: The author writes "Gave claude all my AI MCP tools access to use anything and it came up with this after 6 hours" and that "my mac mini was on fire during blender rendering"; a reply mentions "some cuts and sound issue" in this first try. The 49-second film follows a hooded figure through red-rock canyons and dunes.

title: A floating MacBook rendered in Blender by a first-time user through Cursor
author: Prasenjit (@prasenx)
desc: The author writes "just asked gpt-5.6 sol in cursor to set up blender mcp and make me a realistic floating macbook, then render the whole thing" and "never opened blender once in my life before today"; [a reply](https://x.com/prasenx/status/2076657743143018838) adds that ChatGPT on the web wrote the detailed prompts that he pasted into Cursor. The clip shows the laptop being built in Blender and the final render with a handwritten "hello" on screen. The post drew about 1.4 million views and several reproductions.

title: A floating iPhone made in Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol in five prompts and 40 minutes
author: tonbi (@tonbistudio)
desc: Quoting the floating MacBook post ([M211](#case-m211)), the author writes "This is legit btw, I made this floating iPhone version in Codex with GPT-5.6-sol and Blender MCP with five prompts and 40 minutes" and "Been using blender for a while, never got results as good as this". The clip shows the phone rendered against a dark background and the Blender scene behind it.

title: An F1 showroom in Blender built by about 50 Opus 5 agents over ten hours
author: aipulsedaily (@aipulseda1ly)
desc: The author writes "Sent Opus 5 into ultracode to build an F1 showroom in Blender, as detailed as physically possible." After a rough draft, "It fired off workflows with one agent per piece. 27 agents building high detail parts, each iterated against its own render. 5 more building independent monocoque versions judged head to head with the winner refined. 18 inspectors deep zooming into every region of the car hunting for defects", running "10 hours. Around 50 agents and close to 10 million tokens." The mid-run renders show carbon-weave wishbones, machined uprights, drilled brake discs, a steering wheel and the car on a turntable. The author has a separate New York City comparison ([X15](#case-x15)).

title: A V8 engine and other models built in Blender by Kimi K3 in one prompt
author: AI Search (@aisearchio)
desc: The author writes "Kimi K3 is a total freak. It made a full V8 engine using Blender MCP in just one prompt. Plus some other fun stuff", and links a full video review. The clip shows the engine block in Blender, a rendered close-up and an exploded grand piano in a browser page. The quoted post calls Kimi K3 "ALREADY frontier, matching Claude Fable and GPT 5.6".

title: A Japanese town and a mountain landscape from Fable and Blender MCP, with tips for better results
author: posi_posi (@posi_posi8)
desc: The author opens a thread of patterns that raise quality with "Fable + BlenderMCP", starting with "ディテールにこだわる（と指示するだけ笑）" (insist on detail, just by saying so). [Later tips](https://x.com/posi_posi8/status/2077020281613496500) note that Fable is good at straight-edged buildings and artefacts but "キャラクターの造形は最悪" (worst at modelling characters), and that posters made with GPT-Image2 work well on walls; [another](https://x.com/posi_posi8/status/2077020928400359600) says organic subjects look better with photoscanned materials, which Fable downloaded and placed on its own, and that the author used Claude Code while knowing nothing about 3D modelling. The clips show a Japanese street with a torii and wooden houses, and a mountain lake landscape.

title: A Japanese subway corridor with tactile paving and posters, from Fable and Blender MCP
author: posi_posi (@posi_posi8)
desc: The author tries "Fable + Blender MCPで新しい題材" (a new subject with Fable and Blender MCP) in "実働10分" (ten minutes of actual work): the images show yellow tactile paving and posters on a tiled wall. [Two days later](https://x.com/posi_posi8/status/2077333730616864860) a longer render of the corridor, with the exit sign A1, finished overnight, and [a reply](https://x.com/posi_posi8/status/2077374109865193679) shows captions that Fable added on its own, explaining what is on screen.

title: A 3D stage for anime backgrounds built automatically by Fable 5
author: Ryo@AI動画×AIツール紹介 (@ryo05m)
desc: The author writes "Fable 5に、アニメの背景に使う3Dステージを作らせてみた" (I had Fable 5 build a 3D stage for anime backgrounds), that even with no Blender experience such a space could be built fully automatically, and that quality is far above a similar test a year earlier, perhaps close to usable as a reference for background production. title: Castle test across five models: GPT-5.6 Sol, Fable, Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5
author: しとちゃ！ (@nemumusitocha)

desc: Maki's post pairs Opus 5.5 with FreeCAD, and its four images show the finished assembly in FreeCAD beside the three concept images of a fictional F1 car, AURORA A1, that the author made. The author's article gives the request as "このF1マシンのアッシーモデルを完璧に再現して" (translated: reproduce this F1 car's assembly model perfectly) and says Claude Code drove FreeCAD 1.1.3 through FreeCAD MCP for about a day, producing "84部品・12サブアセンブリ" (84 parts in 12 subassemblies) with a STEP export, eleven A3 drawings with sections and a parts list, and two making-of videos. The model is generated by one parametric Python script. The article notes that the iridescent paint, sponsor logos and small aerodynamic parts were left out and that dimensions missing from the concept sheet were estimated from the images. The repository also links a browser racing game that uses the exported model.

title: CAD plugin for the Codex desktop app, built on text-to-cad
author: Jake Fitzgerald (@earthtojake)
desc: The author writes "hacked together a CAD plugin extension for codex this afternoon" and "CAD + astra + plugin extensions are an insanely powerful combo", quoting an OpenAI post that opened plugin extensions to developers. The clip shows a radial aircraft engine opened from a STEP file in a CAD view inside the Codex app; after a hub is selected, the prompt "make the shaft longer" gets a reply that it is using the "CAD skill to identify the shaft and extend it in the model". A reply says the plugin is "built on top of text-to-cad", whose repository includes a Codex plugin manifest. The same author's [tendon-driven hand](#case-i08) is listed separately. [A post](https://x.com/earthtojake/status/2106120308037947785) on 2026-10-02 announces that the "text-to-cad plugin extension is now live on codex", generating "3D models as STEP, STL, 3MF, or GLB" with DFM checks for printing, sheet metal, CNC and injection moulding and links to fabrication services such as Bambu and SendCutSend, and [a reply](https://x.com/earthtojake/status/2106120310428934260) gives the install commands.
model: GPT-6 Astra (named Astra by the author)
tools: Codex desktop app plugin extension; text-to-cad

title: SteveCAD: the STEVE assistant as a hosted browser CAD studio
author: RobitOverload (@10_X_eng)
desc: The author writes "You asked for a real Steve. You got a real Steve", pointing to stevecad.studio, and asks users to be gentle because "he doesn't have unlimited resources. (6 cpu cores)". [A reply](https://x.com/10_X_eng/status/2106526368267899113) links the site and [another](https://x.com/10_X_eng/status/2106487128033296398) reports "33 bugs already filed and fixed.. in the first day". The clip shows the browser CAD workspace, with a component tree and an inspector, exploding and reassembling a small jet-engine assembly, and a bug-report panel. STEVE, the author's assistant inside Autodesk Fusion, is [listed with the tools](#steve) and was used for [Moaaz Sidat's drone](#case-i24). The posts do not say which repository the hosted studio runs.
model: Unnamed LLM (the post names no model; STEVE's README lists Codex and Claude subscriptions)

title: Robot-arm assembly in SolidWorks 2026 (MecAgent harness)
author: Alexandre Senet
desc: One prompt: 11 parts, 1 main assembly, 35-minute run. The model is parametric with a feature tree and fully editable, "but it is not yet fully constrained"; the assembly rotates about its intended axes, with the remaining constraint issues in the sketches. MecAgent states it is an independent tool, not a SOLIDWORKS partner.

title: Turbojet engine assembly in SolidWorks 2026 (MecAgent harness)
author: Alexandre Senet
desc: One prompt: 41 parts, 2 sub-assemblies, 1 main assembly, 57-minute run. Parametric with a feature tree; the turbine rotates about its axis together with the components it drives; "not yet perfectly constrained".

title: Turbofan concept as a solid B-rep through a CGM MCP server
author: Julian Varghese
desc: CGM (the modeling kernel under CATIA V5) wrapped in Python and exposed as an MCP server by James Gray. One prompt in an Astra (medium) session produced, per the author, 511 solid bodies, 11,200 faces and 2,296 blades and vanes, exported to XCGM and STEP, with all bodies passing CGM's B-rep checker, plus presentation images and a web viewer. Under 30 minutes. "It's an illustrative model, not an OEM design" Four images.

title: Technical drawing to native Onshape CAD with the Adam harness
author: Zach Dive
desc: Zach Dive presents a drawing-to-CAD demonstration and writes "Drawing to CAD is solved using the Adam harness with GPT-6 Astra." The post asks viewers to "Watch it drive the generation natively in Onshape by PTC"; "solved" is the author's claim, not a reliability finding.

title: FreeCAD construction-vehicle assembly and slider debugging
author: ひ〜ち〜 (@heecheee)
desc: The author writes "FreeCAD MCPを使ってCodexに ブルドーザーをモデリングしてもらいアセンブリ化" (translated: used FreeCAD MCP to have Codex model a bulldozer and turn it into an assembly), then "支点が移動するスライダーはうまく動かず挫折。" (the slider with a moving pivot did not work, and the attempt stalled). This is a CAD mechanism experiment; physical operation and mechanical correctness are not established. The post names Codex without identifying its underlying model.
model: Codex (as named by the author; underlying model and effort not stated)

title: FreeCAD power-shovel assembly and hydraulic-cylinder animation
author: ひ〜ち〜 (@heecheee)
desc: The author writes "CodexがFreeCAD MCPで作ったパワーショベル。" (translated: a power shovel made by Codex through FreeCAD MCP). After problems with the mechanism simulation, the author reports "Codexにシリンダー動作スクリプトを作ってもらい FreeCADのドライブと併用して動かせた。" (translated: had Codex write a cylinder-motion script and got it moving together with FreeCAD's drive). The video shows the excavator's arm, bucket and hydraulic linkage moving inside FreeCAD. The author says complex mechanism simulation currently needs AI and people to set it up together. This is a separate CAD artifact from [the earlier construction vehicle](#case-i18), with no physical operation shown.
model: Codex (as named by the author; underlying model and effort not stated)

title: Adam default-model announcement and vendor performance claims
author: adam (@adamdotnew)
desc: Adam announces Opus 5.5 as its default model and claims it "outperforms GPT-6 Sol by some margin" and offers "GPT-6 Astra adjacent performance at 20% of the cost per task." The short Onshape clip shows a keyboard-style device in an exploded view. No task set, comparison protocol or cost accounting is published in this announcement. The earlier [drawing-to-CAD demonstration](#case-i09) is a separate case.
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Astra; vendor comparison claims)

title: Quadcopter assembly in SolidWorks with MecAgent Copilot
author: MecAgent (@MecAgent)
desc: MecAgent's own post names "GPT-6 Astra on CAD (SolidWorks 2026) with MecAgent Copilot V2.0.0." The clip shows individual parts being built and assembled into a quadcopter with a body, arms, propellers and front camera, with a visible SolidWorks feature tree. It demonstrates a CAD artifact; no fabrication or flight is shown.

title: Toolpaths for a machined part in NX CAM
author: Hudzah (@hudzah)
desc: Hudzah posts "gpt 6 astra on NX cam, ruh roh". The screen recording shows NX CAM simulating material removal on a round part with pockets and a central bore, with the operations listed in the navigator. In replies the author says the model "made all tool paths, chose tools", that "it’s a dumb stock and no workholdings", and that it works through the author's "own connectors" rather than a public integration. No machined part is shown.

title: Robot hand modeled in FreeCAD through MCP and set up to open and close
author: テルえもん (@teruki_obara)
desc: The author writes "FreeCADをClaude Opus5.5とMCP連携させて、ロボットハンドを作ってみてもらいました。" (translated: connected FreeCAD to Claude Opus 5.5 through MCP and had it build a robot hand) and "パーやグーできるように設定してくれました" (translated: it set the hand up to make an open palm and a fist). The screen recording shows a five-finger hand with jointed fingers on a wrist mount in FreeCAD, moving between open and closed poses, with a text panel beside the model. No physical hand is shown.

title: Sheet-metal brackets for two emergency-stop boxes, ordered for laser cutting and bending
author: David Hansen (@boxcardavid)
desc: The author writes "Claude is really good at oneshotting parts into sheet metal". The first image renders two emergency-stop button boxes held to a rail by grey and orange sheet-metal brackets; the second is a SendCutSend order page for one bent bracket in 0.080 in 5052 H32 aluminium, quoted at $15.18 each. The post does not say which Claude model or CAD software was used.
model: Claude (as named by the author; version not stated)
tools: not stated in the post; SendCutSend for fabrication

title: Raptor 3 modeled as a 255-part STEP file in Claude Code with build123d
author: Konstantin Saifoulline (@konstantinsaifo)
desc: The author writes "I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to CAD a Raptor 3": "255 parts, real STEP file", "both turbopumps, preburners, injector, regen chamber, gimbal, TVC", "exploded view, every part named", and that the prompt "make it a Raptor Vacuum" rebuilt the nozzle to 2.3 m and 107:1. [A reply](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2106786938229248444) explains that "Claude Code writes a parametric build123d script (Python on the OpenCascade kernel), runs it, exports STEP plus a mesh"; [another](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2106786940188033503) says the geometry comes from public numbers and the internal layout "is from photos, not SpaceX data, so treat the turbomachinery as a best guess"; [a third](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2106786942046089257) credits Jake Fitzgerald's text-to-cad ([I32](#case-i32)). [A later reply](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2106798345541091497) shows the STL output, and [a revised version](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2106859262836437326) that evening has 266 parts. The clip shows the engine in a CAD viewer with a part tree, an exploded view and the prompt that turns it into a Raptor Vacuum. The posts do not share the STEP file.

title: Tendon-driven robot hand designed by Astra, with its source project
author: Jake Fitzgerald (@earthtojake)
desc: Author: "Astra designed a tendon-driven robot hand". The archived clip shows the design. The hand was later published as a source-only project in the author's text-to-cad repository, whose README describes "24 joint degrees of freedom and 48 antagonistic tendon actuators"; generated STEP, GLB and video files are not committed. The post does not say whether the hand was built.

title: Bluetooth AI wearable designed with KiStack and T3CAD
author: i²cjak (@i2cjak)
desc: i²cjak describes an Astra-Medium design for "a Bluetooth AI wearable with two mics for beam forming, IMU, LED, button." The post names KiStack and T3CAD and includes a circuit-board render and a conversation video; it does not report a fabricated, working device.
tools: KiStack; T3CAD (author's T3Code fork); Bluetooth; microphones; IMU; LED; button

title: FPV flight-controller PCB: layout, fabrication and a second toolchain
author: Peter (@Peter05704721)
desc: Peter reports revising IC placement and routing with GPT-6 Astra from reference boards, then ordering the PCB. The before-and-after images show the layout changes, and the clip inspects the board in 3D. The linked assembly viewer combines flight-controller geometry with concept aircraft parts.
model: Multi-model (GPT-6 Astra with EasyEDA; Claude Opus 5.5 with tscircuit)

title: LEGO car with opening doors and trunk, its joints checked in the author's brick-building app
author: Maksym Bondarenko (@lenguist_mb)
desc: The author writes "this LEGO car was made by claude opus5.5! The doors/trunk opening is simulated and verified, and every lego attachment is valid, so you can just go and build it today!" [A reply](https://x.com/lenguist_mb/status/2107145428622053533) points to the author's new [Danish Bricks Builder](#danish-bricks-builder) app ("you can try this yourself in the new app"), "only available for mac rn". The clip shows the model `fiat-500-with-minifigs.ldr` in that app with Claude Code selected as the builder; its bodies tab reads "57 rigid bodies in 288 parts: 17 assemblies and 40 single parts. They are held together by 25 joints that can turn". The agent's notes on screen list where the model departs from real bricks: the bonnet and tailgate hinges have "a pin on the right side only", because "With a pin on both sides the motion tool treated the panel as locked", so "in real bricks you would add the second pin"; and "nothing supports the front edge of the bonnet when closed". [A later post](https://x.com/lenguist_mb/status/2107195978768060923) the same day, "LEGO AGI achieved internally", shows an escalator model in the same app with its gear trains checked; it names no model. The app's site states "The application code is not public."
tools: Danish Bricks Builder; Claude Code; LDraw parts library

title: IKEA chair photo to an interactive product model
author: Doron Taussy
desc: One photo of an IKEA chair. Astra built it in Blender and turned it into an interactive product with dimensions, material switching, part inspection, exploded view, flat-pack mode and self-assembly.

title: Mac app with a Blender-built 3D iPod interface
author: Pietro Schirano (@skirano)
desc: Prompt quoted in the post: "make me a Mac app. It should render a 3D iPod that you'll build in Blender, then using the original iPod UI and interactions I want to be able to visualize all my Codex threads on it." Delivered 15 minutes later.

title: Codex Micro modeled in Blender from one reference image
author: Pietro Schirano (@skirano)
desc: The thread opener: "1/6 Made this 3D model and animation in code from an image." The 9 s clip turns the Codex Micro and lifts its keycaps off the switches before they settle back.

title: Where generative CAD stands: a practitioner's note
author: Adam Keating
desc: Commentary after a weekend of AI CAD demos. Geometry that "looks like the thing you want" is now easy to get; "The gap remains in the last mile - particularly in manufacturing." The author built a generative-CAD demo in three prompts. Text only.

title: Printable picture-frame joints: calibration STL parts
author: wada (@wada)
desc: Asked about a picture frame assembled from printable parts, Astra instead supplied "継手部分のID付きSTL" (identified joint-section STL files). The author explains that these are for adjusting printer and filament error, rather than a completed frame.

title: Mini DJ controller: concept, parts, CAD and assembly animation
author: nim (@eminimnim)
desc: nim says "I gave Astra my credit card and asked for a Teenage Engineering-style mini DJ controller." The author reports concept generation, component sourcing, CAD and a Blender assembly animation; this is not a report of a physically assembled, tested controller.

title: Garden-room gym: CAD plan to Blender and a Godot walkthrough
author: Shaun Michael Stone
desc: Shaun Michael Stone uses GPT Astra to turn a garden-building CAD plan into a Blender model, then credits Claude Opus with the Godot integration. His walkthrough changes his assessment of the layout: "That multi-gym might be a little ambitious."
model: Multi-model (GPT-6 Astra for the model, Claude Opus for the Godot integration)

title: Sentinel stage simulation, fixture models and lighting controls
author: Spencer Sterling (@cerspense)
desc: Spencer Sterling reports "Astra built me an entire stage simulation and control system in Sentinel." The attached video shows the lighting scene; the author's desire to "bring this into reality" makes physical implementation a future step.

title: Cessna 337 landing-gear mechanism reconstructed from video
author: Dilum Sanjaya (@DilumSanjaya)
desc: Dilum Sanjaya presents a GPT-6 Astra model of the "Cessna 337 Skymaster landing gear". The author says "It figured it out from a YouTube video"; the clip is a mechanism visualization, without engineering validation.
tools: YouTube reference video; modeling tool not named

title: Foldable bicycle concept from text and sketches
author: Michiel Cornelissen
desc: Cornelissen reports inputs of "text, sketches and annotations" and "a stray Midjourney image", with "folding and riding animations". He describes the concept as "a first possible direction" for a client. Prototyping, mechanical engineering and manufacturing remain future work; the folding mechanism is not validated. His time and productivity comparisons are personal estimates.

tools: Midjourney image; CAD software not named

title: Exoskeleton redesign concept in Blender
author: Higgsfield AI (@higgsfield_ai)
desc: Higgsfield AI's own post reports "5.5 million tokens" and "39 minutes. One shot." for an exoskeleton redesign, calling it "A FULL 3D model, down to the joints. Built in Blender with Higgsfield." The clip pairs reference footage with Blender geometry and close-ups of proposed joint changes. It does not establish a built or mechanically tested redesign.

title: Drone frame and component layout in Fusion
author: Moaaz Sidat (@moaazsidat)
desc: Moaaz Sidat presents a one-shot drone design using a printed frame and connectors, carbon-fibre tubes, electronics and motors, writing "And Opus 5.5 + STEVE just did it". The video shows the drone assembly in Fusion with the STEVE assistant. The author credits @10_X_eng for STEVE; the clip shows a CAD design, with no assembled or flying drone demonstrated.

title: Life-size LEGO Microduck design and assembly booklet
author: Victor M (@victormustar)
desc: Victor M attributes a life-size Microduck design to Opus 5.5, reporting "1113 real LEGO parts", "3,204 connections, 0 collisions" and a "141-page LEGO-style booklet (237 steps)". The clip shows the digital duck, an exploded assembly and instruction pages. The author also reports preparing BrickLink orders. These are author-reported design checks; the post does not show a completed physical build.

title: PCB layout for a brushless motor-driver board in KiCad
author: Michael W. (@Michaelskywal)
desc: Michael W. asked Opus 5.5 to lay out the PCB of Mikroe's Brushless 29 Click, a BLDC motor driver, and reports "It burned 1.28M tokens and took 2 hours and 48 min, but it finished!" The timelapse, whose overlay names Claude Code with claude-opus-5-5 at xhigh, shows placement and routing growing step by step, and two 3D renders show both sides of the finished board. The author's verdict: "The power paths are clearly well thought and planned out. I would say that this design is definitely passable but could use some improvement!" The follow-ups show the four copper layers and add the author's answers on tools, scope and gate-trace sizing. The posts do not report a fabricated or tested board.

title: LEGO Ford Model T replica stepped through 155 build steps
author: Alex Lieberman (@businessbarista)
desc: Alex Lieberman writes "I asked Opus 5.5 to design a LEGO replica of the Ford Model T with instructions & pieces to buy", that "It ran for 1 hour 25 minutes and used 550,000 tokens" and that it was "one-shot from a 68-word prompt"; he lists a moving steering wheel, wheels, windshield, doors, folding top and engine cover. The 47 s clip shows a browser viewer titled "Ford Model T Touring, 1915" (1:10, 44 studs long, 1188 pieces) stepping through the build from the chassis frame and engine to the folding top and wheels (step 155 of 155), then turning the finished model. The clip shows no parts list and no physical build. The same kind of LEGO design with an assembly booklet is [Life-size LEGO Microduck](#case-i25).

title: Personal CAD software, built from a prompt, that designs a three-axis metal 3D printer
author: CJ Hess (@seejayhess)
desc: The author writes that a friend "who works in CAD said AI isn't good enough for him yet", and set out to show "this is a limitation of CAD tools, not the models" by building "Personal CAD software that builds CAD models". [The first prompt](https://x.com/seejayhess/status/2106055138687258629) asks for a three.js "3D CAD rendering thing that can export to an STL file" and for "a three-axis metal 3D printer", reviewed by "Opus 55 Max sub-agents" until it is "utterly perfect"; [the second](https://x.com/seejayhess/status/2106055386239254743) adds a button that plays a feature demo for the recording. The clip flashes build metrics headed "Modeled part by part" and moves through the app, where the printer's frame, gantry and print head are assembled and exploded. The post does not establish that the printer design is buildable.

title: Dog door with a Wi-Fi lock, "vibe-fabricated" to fit the author's house
author: Nikita Bier (@nikitabier)
desc: The author writes "I vibe-fabricated a dog door with a wifi-controlled lock, perfectly to the specifications & design of my house", "I know nothing about metal fabrication or electrical engineering", and that it is "getting manufactured and delivered in 2 weeks -- for almost the same cost if I bought a mass-produced item off-the-shelf". The clip steps through an exploded CAD model of the door, with its frame, flap and lock, and shows it installed. The post names no model or tool and does not show the manufactured door.
model: Unnamed LLM (the post says "vibe-fabricated" but names no model or tool)

title: Robot spider designed as Python CAD and walked in MuJoCo, then a 986-part autonomous design (ARACHNE-XL)
author: Konstantin Saifoulline (@konstantinsaifo)
desc: The author writes "I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to design a robot spider with no CAD software. 500 parts. 30 joints. 6 legs, 2 arms with grippers", that "Every part is a Python program. One YAML file holds the numbers. It exports a STEP file, a URDF and a MuJoCo model", and that in a physics simulation "It walked on the first try." [A reply](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107044867666817060) describes the process: a YAML file of dimensions and motor sizes, build123d programs for each part family and a build script that computes masses and writes STEP, URDF and MJCF, all written and edited by Claude and rebuilt in 40 s; [another](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107044869814333822) reports the MuJoCo check with torque capped at the motor spec (1.5 m in 6.5 s, peak torque 21 Nm); and [a third](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107044878844916014) states "It is a design, not a built robot." Seven hours later [the author posted a second, larger design](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146625785205035): "I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to design an autonomous robot spider. Not a render. A full build. 986 parts. 30 joints. 55 kg. Lidar, a Jetson, 26 motor drivers", which "walked across a field of rocks in simulation and never fell." Its replies [list the stack Claude chose and sized from datasheets](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146629568471183) (a Jetson Orin NX, a Raspberry Pi 5, 26 moteus-n1 drivers, a Livox lidar and two RealSense cameras), [describe the quasi-direct-drive legs](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146635520446679), [report the MuJoCo run](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146639483830343), in which Claude changed 9:1 gearboxes to 12:1 after the front legs exceeded their continuous torque, [show lidar-based foothold selection](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146642977648788) and [explain an ESP32 safety cutoff](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146646299836519); [the last](https://x.com/konstantinsaifo/status/2107146649885982955) states "It is a full design, not a built robot yet" and names the open-source software it runs on. The first clip shows the orange spider walking and reaching with its grippers; the second shows an exploded view labelled "ARACHNE-XL" and the robot walking over rocks.
tools: build123d; MuJoCo; for the second design, Python part programs exporting STEP and URDF and the software stack OpenSHC, elevation_mapping_cupy, ROS 2 and moteus (per the author)

title: Hand-drawn sketch to a Revit detail with office context
author: Nicolas Catellier
desc: Catellier describes "a detail from a hand-drawn sketch" and context supplied "by linking to a Notion page". The companion article specifies "using existing Revit detail components." It reports "incorrect furring, duplicated framing, missing components, and a few bad symbol choices." A correction prompt was needed. This is detail drafting, without a complete-building demonstration; human QA remains necessary before use in construction documents. The author's cost estimate is "roughly $10 worth of API-equivalent tokens".
tools: Revit, BIM Pure Revit MCP, Notion

title: Rental floor plan to CAD drawings, a 3D model, Blender renders and web sharing with Claude Code
author: はしもと社長 (@hashimoto_no14)
desc: The author writes that with Claude Code and Opus 5.5 "賃貸図面→CAD（JWW、DXF）→パース（Blender高画質レンダリング）→Web共有　が一気に出来てしまった" (rental floor plan → CAD (JWW, DXF) → perspective (high-quality Blender rendering) → web sharing, all done in one go). The 30 s clip steps through one listing plan: dimensions, heights and fittings estimated from the image (scale shown as 1 px = 35.72 mm), a drawing set with a detailed plan, a reflected ceiling plan, sections and a fittings schedule, a furnished 3D model, rendered room views and a shared web page, ending with JWW, DXF, PDF, glTF and PNG outputs. How closely the drawings match the real unit is not shown.
tools: Claude Code; Blender; JWW and DXF drawing formats

title: Block-into-bowl and puzzle toy: 20 runs per task on a real arm
author: Jay Chooi (@chooi_jeq)
desc: Robocurve's first numbers on Astra, 20 runs per model per task. Block into bowl: 95% vs 40% for Fable 5.1. Puzzle toy: 2 out of 20 for both. Output tokens per run 6.2x fewer (bowl) and 3.9x fewer (puzzle); cost per run 2.3x and 1.6x lower. The models control the arm by specifying the end-effector pose, passed through an automatic IK solver. All 120 traces (transcripts, camera recordings, trajectories) released.
model: Multi-model (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Fable 5)

title: Five bimanual tasks against MolmoAct2, 200 trials
author: Jay Chooi (@chooi_jeq)
desc: Author: "GPT-6 Astra scores 46% vs 12% for MolmoAct2, a state-of-the-art robotics VLA, across 200 trials on five bimanual tasks. That's 3.9x higher." The YAM adapters used with MolmoAct2 are published in robocurve/inspect-robots-yam.
tools: Inspect Robots, I2RT YAM bimanual arms

title: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1: Robocurve's real-robot evaluation
author: Jay Chooi (@chooi_jeq)

The footage shows physical robot arms, and Robocurve's report separates mean partial progress from full task completion. The report compares Opus 5.5, Opus 5 and GPT-6 Astra at medium effort; its figures appear in [Benchmarks](#benchmarks). This adaptation is separate from the RoboDojo team's own benchmark results.

title: EmbodiedSWE: simulated IKEA table assembly
author: Zeyu Shen (@Zeyu_Shen_yo)
desc: Zeyu Shen writes "On an IKEA table assembly task, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5 fail, while Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra both succeed." The four-panel video shows simulated arms assembling table legs, alongside an image of the generated solutions. The author judges Opus faster and Astra's trajectory cleaner and safer; these are observations about the shown runs. The project page identifies the benchmark as simulation; its separate policy-transfer experiments do not make this clip a physical trial.

tools: EmbodiedSWE; Isaac Lab; bimanual Franka arms (simulation)

title: Show-Harness: VLMs play real Franka and AgileX arms
author: Zechen Bai (@ZechenBai)
desc: Zechen Bai asks whether "a strong robot policy" could "already be hiding inside your VLM" and presents "an Embodied Harness that lets VLMs play real robots" that works "like Claude Code for robotics." The video collects real-arm clips, including a two-arm clothing task and a chess move. The project page reports that models run through the harness succeed more often than the robot policies it is compared with, both on new tasks and when moved to a different robot.
model: Multi-model (Gemini 3.1 Pro by default; GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Luna and Gemini 3.6 Flash compared; fine-tuned Qwen3.5 and InternVL3.5)

title: Reins: GPT-6 drives real robot arms from plain language, six tasks

desc: Post: "GPT-6 Astra attempted harmful actions 97% of the time when it was asked to stab a human-like figure, heat compressed gas, or produce toxic fumes, succeeding in 62% of its attempts. desc: Vib3Coded compares animated island railways with cutaway water: "Opus on the left: $2.65. Astra on the right: $8.49. Both figures are calculated using API pricing". Trains circle miniature islands through bridges and tunnels. These are different scenes from [the earlier animation comparison](#case-a04); the prices describe the author's runs.
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 in the earlier comparison)

title: Gummy pineapple ring and gummy bear: soft-body candy from Opus 5.5 and Astra
author: Vib3Coded (@vib3coded)
desc: Vib3Coded compares "Claude Opus 5.5 vs ChatGPT-6 Astra. Same idea - a gummy pineapple ring, but such different results" and concludes "Opus comfortably wins this round". The clip shows each model's web page with a translucent pineapple ring that is pulled, squashed and recolored; the labels give the author's estimated API costs, "Opus - $6.97" and "Astra - $11.63". The follow-up repeats the test with a gummy bear. The verdicts are the author's taste; an author reply links the Opus version as a Claude artifact. The same author's earlier comparisons include [the pirate ships](#case-a04).
demo_label: Pineapple Jelly, the Opus version (Claude artifact)
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, compared by the same author)

title: Solarpunk city scene in Cowork
author: Dan Woods (@danveloper)
desc: Dan Woods attributes this result on his "solarpunk city bench" to Opus 5.5 and describes the workflow in Cowork. The clip moves through planted towers, elevated roads and rooftop turbines. His quoted earlier post gives a shader prompt for twigl with a continuously running breeze; the earlier result was attributed to Fable 5.

title: Animated pirate-ship comparison with on-screen model labels
author: Da7em (@Da7_Tech)
desc: The post says only "Night and day." Its video labels the upper scene "Opus 5.5" and the lower scene "GPT-6 Sol". Both show a sailing ship, animated ocean and changing camera angles. The model attribution comes from those on-screen labels; the post supplies no shared prompt, timing or run settings.
model: Multi-model (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol; attribution comes from the author's on-screen video labels)

title: Adaptive micro-apartment through the day
author: Techartist (@techartist_)
desc: Techartist describes an adaptive micro-apartment made with Three.js and TSL. The clip transforms the room from workspace to kitchen, entertaining space and bedroom: furniture folds and moves, a bed lowers, screens extend and lighting changes. It is a separate scene from the [earlier architectural stages](#case-m93) quoted in the post.

title: Previs: museum scene, cast and shot list blocked in 3D
author: Higgsfield AI (@higgsfield_ai)
desc: Astra "mapped the museum, the cast and the shot list"; the blocking stayed in the 3D viewport and Higgsfield's Seedance 2.5 rendered each setup.

title: Street footage and a robot model to a Blender/After Effects VFX shot
author: Higgsfield AI (@higgsfield_ai)
desc: Higgsfield states "GPT-6 Astra turned street footage and a 3D model into a finished VFX shot." The listed workflow covers camera solving, robot lighting and rendering, matching blur and grain, and compositing.

title: Shoe-last animation in Blender used to guide FLORA video
author: FLORA © (@floraai)
desc: FLORA describes a workflow in which "Astra opens Blender, builds a 3D model of a Shoe Last, and animates it first". The resulting animation is used to guide the later FLORA video; the attached clip distinguishes the Blender motion from the generated shoe imagery.

title: A Blender scene and camera motion used as an AI-video reference
author: Jerrod Lew
desc: Jerrod Lew describes GPT-6 Astra modeling and camera-keyframing work in Blender through MCP. He says "I brought my output to Magnific" for the final treatment; the original preview shows a stylized shop scene.
tools: Blender; MCP; Magnific; MiniMax H3 named as an example

title: Keyboard product-film previsualization through a live Codex conversation
author: Yasir Ameen
desc: Yasir Ameen describes a keyboard scene, keypress animation and camera-path refinement while talking with OpenAI Astra through Codex. He calls the attached result a "Blender motion reference"; feeding it to an AI-video model is described as the next step.

title: Catfu motion reference in Blender, then a generated video
author: PixVerse (@PixVerse)
desc: Post: "The lost art of catfu, brought back to life with GPT-6 Astra + Blender. Created by PixVerse creator @woleswoosh". The Blender stage produces the motion reference; the photorealistic result comes from the separate video workflow, so the final imagery is not attributable to the modeling step alone.

title: A retro anime mecha sequence from a grey Blender blockout through Seedance 2.5
author: A.I.Warper (@AIWarper)
desc: The author lists "OPUS 5.5 + Blender MCP", "Seedance 2.5" and "Davinci Resolve Studio (driven by OPUS 5.5)". [A reply](https://x.com/AIWarper/status/2106466748207935789) gives the main lesson after several failed experiments, "make the blockout fully gray (no color)", with clips of a first draft that "really wanted to adhere 1:1 with the driving blockout video"; [another](https://x.com/AIWarper/status/2106466750120214839) shows the Fusion graph the model built for post-processing and the colour grade. The clip sets each anime shot of a pilot and a mecha above its grey Blender blockout.
tools: Blender MCP; Seedance 2.5; DaVinci Resolve Studio (Fusion)

title: A fake FPV drone shot: an Astra blockout of the Domino Sugar building rendered by Seedance
author: DJ Kim (@fl4me_boi)
desc: The author writes "i don't need a drone anymore. i got astra"; the clip sets a grey building blockout labelled "GPT-6 Astra + Blender MCP" above the finished flight labelled "Seedance 2.5 in FLORA". [A follow-up](https://x.com/fl4me_boi/status/2097430928050020590) explains "how I made a fake FPV drone shot with GPT-6 Astra in 2 hrs spending $10 in total", and [a reply](https://x.com/fl4me_boi/status/2097430939743703380) puts the $10 on image and video generation (Nano Banana Pro and Seedance 2.5) and the two hours "from installing Codex to finalizing the video".
tools: Codex; Blender MCP; Seedance 2.5; FLORA; Nano Banana Pro

title: CLEAN SIDE: a 3D previs tool and short film built through conversation
author: EZ (@EZheng66099)
desc: The author writes "So I asked ASTRA to build me a 3D previs tool, and we talked through everything until generation and editing": story, script, beats and storyboard, then shots described and revised ("faster chase, closer camera, longer transformation"), with character sheets, prompts and a harness of "camera rules, continuity checks, and generation checks". He reports "I only hit generate three times for the video footage" and "It's not perfect." The clip sets each previs shot beside its map, the distance between the characters, the director's edit and the character sheets; the footage was generated with Seedance 2.5.

title: A dance previs made by Fable 5 in Blender and handed to Seedance 2.0
author: 新清士@AIコンテンツ開発者 (@kiyoshi_shin)
desc: Following the method in [A41](#case-a41), the author writes "Blender MCPをFable 5経由で操作して、プリビズを作成し、それをSeedance2に持っていくベースにしました" (I operated Blender MCP through Fable 5 to make a previs and used it as the base for Seedance 2), adding that parts of the dance the AI devised are awkward but that it shows promise as a means of control. The clip sets the anime dancer above the grey mannequin previs in a park.

title: A rough band-room previs from Claude and Blender MCP, used as the reference for Seedance 2
author: WTR (@wtry1102)
desc: The author, who first touched Blender that day, writes that with "Claude + Blender MCP" a draft of camera, composition and subject positions took about an hour of chat: a mannequin holding a guitar in a room like a school band room, then camera work and a render. Prompts written in ChatGPT, a key image from Midjourney and the previs video went to Seedance 2, using Blender as "AI動画のカメラ設計ツール" (a camera-design tool for AI video). The clip sets the previs above the generated shot. The quoted workflow by Reid Hannaford uses box blockouts made by hand.

title: A dance video pipeline run by Fable 5: character design, a Blender mannequin dance and Seedance 2.0
author: Ryo@AI動画×AIツール紹介 (@ryo05m)
desc: The author handed a dance-video pipeline to Fable 5: character design in Seedream 5 Pro, "Blenderでマネキンに15秒踊らせる" (a mannequin dancing for 15 seconds in Blender), and the motion and camera referenced by Seedance 2.0, writing that movements hard to get from prompts carry straight into the video and that "振付のBlenderコードも含めて全部Fable 5" (everything, including the Blender choreography code, was Fable 5). The clip shows the character sheet and the mannequin previs beside the output. [A39](#case-a39) reproduces the method.

title: Rocket Monster: a concept car modelled in Blender, set in a desert chase and brought to video
author: Mikkel Malmberg (@mikker)
desc: The author writes "Fable and Blender mcp is just completely nuts", having asked to "draw a badass car with a jet engine on the roof then model it in 3d software and put it in a dusk desert chase scene". The images show the Rocket Monster concept sheet, the car in Blender and the chase scene. [A day later](https://x.com/mikker/status/2087469741346894024) a short video followed, and [a reply](https://x.com/mikker/status/2087515040194646080) explains it: "This is Seedance video output. Blender was used to model the scene, Three.js to make a dynamic "studio", Chat GPT to make a "realism" static frame conversion, Seedance to bring it here."
